title: Tool offer
description: The tools the host offers a run, as the session's two members: the runtime's tools (session.tools: McpTool, exactly as tools/list served them, filtered to this session's allow-list, reached only through callTool and the host's gate) and the host's own tools (session.hostTools: HostTool, run by the host on the adapter's behalf, answered in the shape a runtime answer takes). An adapter offers the model exactly these, under their served schemas (servedSchema: a tool served without an input schema ends the session; the Gemini family alone is shown the schema less a closed list of keywords, with a guardrail narrowed event per tool that lost one). The host also adds its own context tools (list_context, read_context, read_window and, in a conversation, update_plan and request_budget_increase), whose names an offered tool may not take. Read from web/src/assistant/engine.ts (McpTool, HostTool) and context/session.ts (contextualSession). Open: the session is an in-process value with no reader, and the runtime's answer is passed through as served. A host may offer propose_pack ($defs/proposePack): the adapter reads that call itself as the run's proposal and never reaches the host's execute, the instructions then tell the model to use it, the critic is not offered it, and the fenced block stays the fallback. The critic is offered only $defs/criticTools, of the runtime tools the session offers, and no host tool (agent#10). Tool sources (ADR-0006): a host tool that a source outside the host serves (a gateway connection, a public MCP server, a tool the person created) is declared with its source record ($defs/sourceDeclaration) and is still a host tool: the host executes it under the person's grants and the package never reaches the source. The package offers it under a wire-safe name mapped to the source and its own name ($defs/wireName, $defs/nameMapping), with its description bounded and framed as retrieved text, its effect class and approval default ($defs/effectClass), and, where the source's tools pass the schema budget, as a catalogue entry whose schema load_tool loads ($defs/catalogueEntry, $defs/loadTool). Skills (ADR-0009): the host declares skills beside its host tools (skills, $defs/skillDeclaration, skill.json): the package admits each, lists the admitted ones in the system text after the tools described in text ($defs/skillCatalogueEntry), and offers load_skill and unload_skill beside load_tool ($defs/loadSkill, $defs/unloadSkill) where any is catalogued; a loaded skill ($defs/loadedSkill) rides after the history, and grants no tool. The critic's switch (ADR-0010) rides beside them: critic, criticProject, criticReasoning, existingPack, reviewerAssigned, each optional.

tools.description: The runtime's tools (session.tools), each named within the ceiling.

hostTools.description: The host's tools (session.hostTools), the context tools the boundary adds included.

skills.description: The skills the host declares for the run (ADR-0009), beside hostTools: each a skill with the digest the person approved ($defs/skillDeclaration). Absent or empty, the run has no skills catalogue and no load_skill.

critic.description: The run's word on the critic (ADR-0010; the person's, from the host's per-run control): off, auto or on. It wins over the project's word (criticProject) and the policy table's (policy.critic.default). Absent, the run states none. adversarialReview is retired in v0.9.1 and refused on presence; use critic.

criticProject.description: The project's word on the critic (ADR-0010), as the host passes it from the project's settings: off, auto or on. Read where the run states none; absent, the policy table's default (policy.critic.default) decides.

criticReasoning.description: The critic's reasoning tier (ADR-0010), in the enum of the run's capability: a thinking tier (off, on, ultra) on the model capability, an effort (none to max) on the agent capability; a value of the other capability's enum is refused before any request (configuration). Absent, the critic runs at the author's tier (budget.json criticReasoningFloor, author). A value lower than the author's is the host's explicit choice: it is honoured and recorded in critic_decided and the checkpoint's critic.

existingPack.description: The host's fact that the run works on a pack that already exists rather than drafting a new one (ADR-0010): under auto, a proposal of such a run changes an existing pack, one of the three triggers. Absent is false.

reviewerAssigned.description: The host's fact that a human reviewer is assigned to the run's work (ADR-0010): the critic does not run in any mode, with the reason reviewer-assigned. Absent is false.

runtimeTool.description: A runtime tool (McpTool). No effect class is carried: the host decides what is read-only by name (runtimeToolContextPolicy and the read list in context/managed.ts).

inputSchema.description: The runtime's own JSON Schema for the arguments, passed through untouched.

hostTool.description: A host tool's declaration (HostTool, without its execute function, which never crosses). Its schema is the host's, written in the subset every family's wire carries.

effect.description: Host-declared effect, never supplied by model arguments.

interaction.description: A tool the adapter handles itself. question (ask_user): the adapter emits user_question, pauses, and returns no answer of its own. delegation (delegate_tasks): the host's coordinator runs the batch; an engine that awaits a tool call (vercel) executes it in the run's step with no tool-call deadline and reports a tool_call and a tool_result, the children's findings its result (agent#14); an engine whose run cannot wait for one (codex) emits delegation_requested and ends its run.

delegation.description: The read-only capability this tool offers to a delegated child; absent means parent-only.

contextPolicy.description: Host-declared context retention (ContextToolPolicy), independent of topic, provider and action permission. immutable: the same arguments return the same value, so a read may be served from the read cache: the run's own, or a chat-scoped context's across the chat's runs (agent#8, tool-result.json#/$defs/readCacheKey); declare it only for a value that does not change for the same arguments while the chat lasts. reference: prefer this material in the bounded working summary. runtime: the result depends on the Runtime that serves it (its identity and version), so a chat's read cache keys it by the Runtime the host names for the run; every runtime tool is.

presentation.description: Host-owned presentation, frozen when the tool is offered.

source.description: Where the tool comes from (ADR-0006), on a tool a source outside the host serves; absent on the host's own tools. On the offer it carries tool, the tool's own name at its source.

approval.description: Whether a call needs the person's approval before the host runs it (ADR-0006, ADR-0008): the host's approval policy (HostTool.approve, Go ApprovalPolicy) answers each call at once, $defs/approvalPolicy: allow runs it, refuse refuses it (the model reads a refused result and a guardrail says why), ask pauses the run (run-event.json#/$defs/approval_requested) until the person decides. A required tool without a policy answers ask. none: the call runs without asking, the host's declared decision. Default by effect class: none for read and propose (a proposal's approval is its review card), required for act. Read on a tool with a source; the host's own tools keep their own rules.

proposePack.description: The host tool through which the model delivers its proposal (packages/harness/engines/contract.ts: PROPOSE_PACK_TOOL, PROPOSE_PACK_SCHEMA). The host registers it among its hostTools under this name and with this input schema, which is in the subset every family's wire carries. The adapter reads the call's arguments as the proposal under the fence's rules (documentJson required as complete JSON document text, legacy document refused, unknowns strings, kind absent or create), answers the model that it was received, and never calls the host's execute; arguments of another shape are a failed result naming what to correct (invalid-tool-input). The latest call's document is the one proposed. A fenced proposal in the same answer makes it ambiguous, refused as two fenced proposals are; a later request of the turn that fails leaves it delivered with a note (run-event.json, proposal).

documentJson.description: The complete proposed pack as JSON document text. Numeric values that change during canonical serialization are refused; decimal spelling and negative zero may normalize.

unknowns.description: What the policy leaves open, one sentence each.

agentWireTool.description: A tool as the codex engine offers it on the agent wire (codexbridge.Tool in the start frame's request): an alias name desk_runtime_N or desk_host_N, the real name prefixed to the description, and the served schema. Closed: the Desk server decodes the start frame with unknown members refused; a request carries at most 128 tools.

inputSchema.description: The served schema, which the Desk server requires to be a JSON object whose type is object, at most 64 KiB (65536 bytes) as JSON text; a description is at most 8192 bytes, and all tools' schemas and descriptions together at most 1 MiB (codexbridge threadParams).

runtimeCeiling.description: The runtime tools any session may be allowed (ASSISTANT_TOOLS in packages/harness/host.ts). A session's allow-list is a subset; the gate refuses a call outside it on the wire. The Desk's five (runtimeToolCeiling in contract/desk/inventory.json) and, from the harness (agent#7), experimental_test_cases, which takes pack text and a matrix and reads no project file; it leaves the page only with the arguments tool-call.json $defs/testCasesArguments states, and one turn may call it at most testCallsPerTurn times (budget.json). The Runtime's other test and project tools stay off it: test_conformance (its suite argument is a local path the runtime reads), experimental_test_packs and experimental_test_graphs (they test the saved tree, not the draft, outside the rehearsal rule), get_pack and list_packs (they read the saved tree); toolGate.ts, REFUSED_RUNTIME_TOOLS.

reservedName.description: Names the host keeps for its own context tools; an offered tool that takes one ends the session (context/session.ts, contextualSession). read_window (agent#1) and search (agent#5) are the harness's own readers. load_tool (ADR-0006) is the harness's catalogue loader, offered only where the schema budget trips. load_skill and unload_skill (ADR-0009) are the harness's skill loaders, offered only where the run catalogues a skill. request_review (ADR-0010) is the harness's ask for a review, offered only under auto in the author's phase.

criticTools.description: The critic's tools (agent#10; packages/harness/refutation.ts, CRITIC_TOOLS and CRITIC_READERS): an allow-list, and the whole of what the critic may call. Four of the runtime's reads about the document: validate, experimental_evaluate (only as a rehearsal, the gate's rewrite) and get_schema, and experimental_test_cases under its own bounds (tool-call.json $defs/testCasesArguments, and budget.json testCallsPerTurn, which the critic shares with the loop). Then two of the harness's own context readers, read_window and search (review row 6): the context ledger's tools, whose names a host tool may not take ($defs/reservedName), which reach no Runtime tool and no action; with them the critic reads its own first message where that message was retained to fit its request. The critic is offered these, of the tools the session offers, in the session's order. Any other name it calls (the runtime's other reads, every host tool, propose_* and request_* among them, and the other context tools) is refused by the shared boundary while the critic runs (context/session.ts, admit on the wrapped callTool and host tools), before the tool gate and before a host tool runs: the call is not made, the model reads a permission failure, and a guardrail refused event names the tool. Where the run catalogues skills (ADR-0009), the critic is also offered load_skill and unload_skill: a skill grants no tool, so a load leaves this list as it is.

effectClass.description: What a call of a tool with a source may do (ADR-0006): read (it only reads; its result is data), propose (it is never run during the run: the call is held as a proposal for the person's review card, as propose_pack's is, and the host runs it on acceptance, after the run, under its grants) or act (it changes something outside the run, and by default needs the person's approval before each call). A tool with a source is act, with approval required, unless the host declares it a read or a proposal; the model's arguments never change it. On the offer the package sets the host tool's effect from it: read is effect read, propose is effect proposal, act is no effect, so Plan mode and a delegated child, which admit reads only, never offer an act.

approvalPolicy.description: What the host's approval policy answers for one act call (ADR-0008; HostTool.approve, Go ApprovalPolicy), asked with the call (the wire name, the tool's own name, its source record, a copy of the arguments) and answered at once, never waiting for the person: allow, the call runs under its bounds; refuse, it is refused with a guardrail (reason approval refused) and never run; ask, the run pauses (approval_requested). An answer that is none of the three, or a policy that fails, is refuse.

identity.description: The identity a source's calls run as (ADR-0019): person, service or connection, and a label the person recognises. The label is display text, never a credential or token, and grants nothing. The host declares it per source; where it says nothing the package uses connection and the source id as the label. The package shows it, records it and counts calls by it; the model never chooses it.

sourceRecord.description: Where a host tool comes from (ADR-0006). Declared by the host on each host tool a source outside the host serves; the package adds tool (the tool's own name at its source) on the offer, carries the record on the tool's tool_call and tool_result events (with receipt on a result where the host's answer gave one), and counts the source in the run report (provenance.json#/$defs/sourceFigures). gateway: a gateway connection the person configured (Databricks, Azure DevOps, Drive), which may give a receipt for each call; mcp: a public MCP server the host connected, whose tool list is pinned by digest at connection time; custom: a tool the person created; exchange (ADR-0009): a skill whose bytes the host fetched from a Judgment Exchange entry, the entry's id and version the record's id and version, which a host tool may not declare. runtime is the Runtime's own row in the run report: its tools come through tools/list behind the gate, carry no declaration, and a host tool declared with kind runtime is refused. Either version or toolListDigest is present; mcp carries toolListDigest. Closed: the package refuses another member before any request (configuration).

id.description: The source's name as the host names it (a connection, a server, the person's own tools): a letter, then letters, digits and hyphens, at most 24 characters. Every wire name of the source's tools begins with it.

version.description: The source's version as the host knows it: a connection's revision, a server's version, a custom tool's revision.

trust.description: The trust class the host gives the source: first-party (the Runtime, and a source the host itself runs), connected (a connection the person configured with their own grants), public (a public server), person (a tool the person wrote). Reported, never a grant: whatever the class, the source's descriptions are untrusted text and its results data, and its tools are held to their effect class.

identityDigest.description: The package's pin of identity: sha256: then the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of identity. It is set with the source's tool-list pin and compared with the identity the host reports before a call; a change withholds the source until the person re-approves it.

tool.description: The tool's own name at its source, set by the package on the offer and the events from the declaration's name (the wire name is the offered tool's name). A declaration leaves it out.

receipt.description: On a tool_result only: the receipt id the host's answer gave for this call (HostToolResult.receipt; a gateway connection's), at most 128 characters.

toolListDigest.description: The digest of a source's tool list (ADR-0006): sha256: then the SHA-256, lower-case hex, of the UTF-8 text of the canonical JSON (tool-result.json#/$defs/readCacheKey's: members sorted by name in UTF-16 code units, no whitespace, strings and numbers as JSON.stringify writes them) of the list of the source's tools, each {name, description, inputSchema} as the source serves it (description the empty string where it has none), ordered by name in UTF-16 code units (toolListDigest in toolSources.ts; Go runcontext.ToolListDigest). An mcp source's declaration carries the digest the person approved, pinned when the host connected the server. The package computes the digest of the tools the host declares for the source and, where the two differ, offers none of the source's tools; mid-run, where the host's source.currentDigest() answers another digest before a call, that call and every later call of the source are refused and never run. Only a new declaration with the new digest, which the person's re-approval gives the host, lifts it.

wireName.description: The name the model is shown for a tool with a source, and the offered tool's name (ADR-0006). Provider wires take [A-Za-z0-9_-], at most 64 characters, and no colon. The rule (wireName in toolSources.ts; Go runcontext.WireName): every character of the tool's own name outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] becomes _; the name is the source's id, two underscores, then that. Where nothing was replaced and the result is at most 64 characters, that is the wire name; otherwise its first 55 characters, an underscore and the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the source's id, a line feed and the tool's own name (UTF-8), so two names that differ only in replaced characters, or past the 64th, get different wire names whatever their order. A wire name that still equals another offered name (another source's tool, a host tool, a Runtime tool, a reserved name) is refused: every tool that bears it is withheld, with a guardrail refused event naming it.

nameMapping.description: One row of the offer's mapping (ADR-0006): the wire name the model sees and calls, the source's id and the tool's own name there. Stable: the same source and name give the same wire name in every run, whatever else is declared.

sourceDeclaration.description: A host tool with a source, as the host declares it (ADR-0006): its own name at the source (name, 1 to 128 characters), its description and schema as the source serves them, its source record, and optionally its effect class and approval. A declaration whose record or members are not these, or which carries effect or interaction (the package sets effect from effectClass; a source's tool is never a question or a delegation), or delegation on anything but a read, is refused before any request (configuration). A declaration whose name is a Runtime tool's (runtimeCeiling, and the Runtime tools kept off it), a reserved name, load_tool or propose_pack is withheld from the offer with a guardrail refused event: a Runtime's tools reach the model only through the gate.

catalogueEntry.description: A tool with a source as the offer shows it where the source was made a catalogue (ADR-0006): where the tools with a source pass offeredSchemas or offeredSchemaBytes (budget.json), sources are made catalogues, the largest first (by its tools offered, then by their bytes, then by id), until the rest fit. A catalogued tool is offered with its wire name; the words "Catalogued tool: call load_tool with this name for its schema before calling it.", then its description's first line, cut to 160 bytes and framed as retrieved text; and an open schema, so the request's tools, and the stable prefix with them, never change during the run. The model asks load_tool for the real schema ($defs/loadTool); a call of a catalogued tool whose schema the run has not loaded is refused (invalid-tool-input) and never run.

loadTool.description: The harness tool that loads one catalogued tool's schema (ADR-0006): a reserved name, offered only where the run's tools with a source pass the schema budget, and admitted only for a catalogued wire name (any other is invalid-tool-input). Its answer ($defs/loadedSchema) is data and framed as such; the loaded schema then rides in the execution state, after the history, on every later request of the run, as one data block, so the stable prefix holds. Loaded schemas count against offeredSchemaBytes: a load past it is tool-failed and nothing is loaded.

name.description: The catalogued tool's name, as the tools list shows it.

loadedSchema.description: What load_tool answers for one catalogued tool (ADR-0006), before it is framed: its wire name, its source record with its own name, its description bounded by toolDescriptionBytes, and its schema as declared (narrowed on the Gemini family's wire as every offered schema is).

skillDeclaration.description: A skill as the host declares it (ADR-0009, skill.json): the bundle, its source record and the digest the person approved (pinnedDigest), and no digest of its own (the package computes it). A declaration the package cannot read (skill.json's members and bounds, a source of kind runtime, two skills of one name or one id, a source declared twice with different records) ends the run before any request (configuration). A readable one is withheld from the catalogue, with a guardrail refused event whose reason is skill withheld, where a tools[] name is not a host tool the host declared for the run, where its bytes pass skillBytes, or where its bundle does not hash to pinnedDigest (until the person re-approves it).

skillCatalogueEntry.description: One admitted skill as the skills catalogue in the system text lists it (ADR-0009): its name, then its description's first line, cut to 160 bytes and framed as retrieved data under the run's marker. The catalogue sits after the tools described in text, in the stable prefix: it never changes during the run, and a load or an unload changes neither it nor the tool list. Its entries, in the order declared, are held to cataloguedSkills and skillsCatalogueBytes (each counted as the JSON text of its name and its line, the frame's constant lines not counted); the skills past either are withheld, one guardrail for each source saying how many.

loadSkill.description: The harness tool that loads one catalogued skill (ADR-0009): a reserved name, offered beside load_tool where the run catalogues any skill, in Plan mode and to the critic too (a skill grants no tool), never to a built-in child; declared children receive only the skills their definition names. Its effect is plan, so its answer is not framed as data. It loads only a catalogued, admitted skill (any other name is invalid-tool-input); each load counts against skillsPerRun, the response's loads carried through a resume in the run report's rows (provenance.json#/$defs/sourceFigures, skills), and a load past it is refused (tool-failed, not-started) with a guardrail whose reason is skill budget. Loading a skill already loaded loads nothing and counts nothing. A load emits skill_loaded, writes the checkpoint's skills, and the skill's instructions and resources ride after the history on every later request as one block, under the heading that ranks them with the project's own instructions; on the agent wire, which sends the execution state once per run, the answer carries the block itself. Its answer: the loaded skill ($defs/loadedSkill), its bytes, and a note.

name.description: The skill's name, as the skills catalogue lists it.

unloadSkill.description: The harness tool that drops one loaded skill (ADR-0009): a reserved name, offered with load_skill. The skill's block leaves every later request, skill_unloaded is emitted and the checkpoint's skills is written; the skill stays catalogued, and loading it again counts again. A name not loaded is invalid-tool-input.

loadedSkill.description: A skill as a load names it (ADR-0009): its id, its name, its source record and its digest. load_skill's answer and the skill_loaded event carry it; the instructions are never on the event.

criticMode.description: The critic's switch (ADR-0010): off, the critic never runs; on, it runs on every proposal; auto, it runs on a proposal where the package's own facts say so (declared cases exist, the proposal changes an existing pack, or the model asked through request_review). The mode is the run's word, else the project's, else the policy table's (run > project > table).

criticReasoning.description: A reasoning tier in the enum of a run's capability (ADR-0010): the thinking tiers off, on and ultra of the model capability (ThinkingTier), or the efforts none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh and max of the agent capability (CodexEffort), each enum in its own order, lowest first.

requestReview.description: The harness tool by which the model asks for a review (ADR-0010): a reserved name, offered only where the critic's mode is auto, in the author's phase, on a run the critic is not forced off for; never offered to the critic, to a delegated child, in Plan mode or to the reformat run. It takes one optional reason. The first call of a run is recorded as the trigger model-asked (the checkpoint's critic, carried through a resume) and answered with a note; the package then runs the critic on the run's proposal. A second call of the run, a call under off or on, and a call outside the author's phase are refused (tool-failed, not-started) with a guardrail whose reason is review refused, and nothing is recorded. The model's ask is a trigger, never a verdict: it cannot turn a review off or decide what the critic finds. Its effect is plan, so its answer is not framed as data.

reason.description: Why a review of this run’s proposal is wanted, in one sentence.

remember.description: Propose memory for the person to review, never store or accept. Author only, including Plan mode; child and critic calls refused. UTF-8 text bounded by memoryProposalBytes, count by memoryProposalsPerRun across resume.

propose_edit.description: ADR-0015: change only the package draft. Author only. Anchors must occur exactly once; every candidate, including undo, is validated before replacement.

propose_delete.description: ADR-0015: change only the package draft. Author only. Anchors must occur exactly once; every candidate, including undo, is validated before replacement.

propose_insert.description: ADR-0015: change only the package draft. Author only. Anchors must occur exactly once; every candidate, including undo, is validated before replacement.

undo_edit.description: ADR-0015: change only the package draft. Author only. Anchors must occur exactly once; every candidate, including undo, is validated before replacement.

draftId.description: The current package-owned document in the search/read_window id space; the suffix is its document id, never a file path.
